limitations: Reviewer is a separate AI agent session on the same host and the same operator account as the producer. It is not a second machine, a second operator, or a human. It ran no harness, used no network, changed no git state and no repository file, and read nothing outside the repository and the code snapshot (stated commit 1860ade; the snapshot holds no git data, so the commit id was not checked). It never read the vendor home. The work was done in three rounds by the same reviewer id; this round is a delta review of set v3 against set v2.

Two earlier sets were rejected by this reviewer. Set v1 (80.8): it called the root complete, but only two environment variables were redirected, HOME was the operator's home, and retained metadata showed that a shared vendor store (~/.cursor/ai-tracking/ai-code-tracking.db) changed 29 ms after the scored edit of run 3; portable.complete_root and three native_absent rows were unproven. Set v2 (78.1): the root defect was fixed, but the new public shared-store extract held 18 short vendor line hashes with an unknown preimage that differs between runs and may cover the private file path; this broke the bound-digest rule. Set v3 zeroes these values and the row ids. A defect that this reviewer cannot see may still exist.

The captures were made by the producer on 2026-10-06, after the rule changes of 2026-10-03 to 2026-10-05. Runs r1, r2, r3 are the first three attempts of that day with build 2026.10.01-e373342 and the only cursor-cli-2026-10-06 attempts; older attempts with another build are disclosed in the adapter document. Capture completeness and acquisition authenticity are the producer's retained receipts, not facts witnessed by the reviewer.

Root. portable.complete_root is a contradiction (0 of 3), as for Codex CLI and Antigravity: rows of each session sit in a shared store that holds other sessions and cannot be copied whole. portable.companions is measured for the id-named family (store.db, meta.json, transcript). The release code records the blocker portable_archive:hard_gate for each repetition; it does not block the rank, as for those two rows.

Absence path. attribution.usage, attribution.token_semantics and attribution.reconciliation are native_absent without a complete root, under the rubric sentence of 2026-10-05 (complete id-named family plus the bound rows of every shared store that names the session). The shared-store rows were read after the captures from the live store by the coordinator, by owner permission, for the three test sessions only. They are bound by content (session id, call id and path of the native edit, times inside the native edit step, content hash equal to the native post-edit hash), not by a capture-time hash. The list of tables of the store is the coordinator's statement. The reviewer checked the extract against public and private native bytes and against the retained metadata inventory, but could not compare it with the store. Inside the two redirected directories the reviewer searched every blob with its own wire reader, the meta row, the sidecar, the transcript and the two harness files: no token count exists; root field 5 is a context-size estimate without an output count.

No capture-time bracket. The controller of these runs took no inventory before or after. The vendor home was listed once by metadata 449 s after run 3 (for another purpose): no entry changed in the run 1 and run 2 windows, two in the run 3 window (the store and its directory), and 154 later entries belong to a later desktop start and could hide an earlier write. Locations outside the vendor home and the two redirected directories (application support, caches, temporary directories, keychain) were never inventoried; writes there cannot be ruled out. The reviewer accepts this for ranking by the standard of the ranked Codex CLI and Antigravity rows, which ran in the operator's home and listed only the vendor state directory. A reader who requires a bracket would hold the three absence rows unresolved; the row would then be provisional (78.1 to 90.1). The emptiness of the two directories at the start rests on the controller code.

Judgments that carry points. (1) The injected context message (about 45 KB, role user, in no turn of the turn tree) is classified system. Counted as a prompt, as the Codex row counts its context message, density would be about one point higher and duplicate safety about 0.05 higher. (2) A root row with a pending assistant message takes the role of that message and counts with its whole row, as every record of every configuration does; counting only the pending message would lower the score by 0.09 to 0.13 points, counting only the call parts by 0.26 to 0.29. (3) Old checkpoint roots count as occurrences; a read from the latest root only would add about 0.07. (4) broad.standard_tools_readable is 0 because order, times, call records and the exact prompt are protobuf blobs without a published schema, as for Antigravity. (5) Version rows (4 points): meta.json schemaVersion 1 and PRAGMA user_version 1; the decoder refuses another value; only one value of each was ever observed, and no version covers the protobuf field layout.

Model identity. The model name (cursor-grok-4.5-high) comes from the JSON message that states the same response. The two statements are joined by position in the turn and equal text, with call ids on neighbouring parts, not by a key. The stream names only the route (Auto). This is the vendor's own statement; no independent channel confirms which model served the calls.

Transcript. The transcript is in the read because the absence scan opens it. It has no ids; its lines are bound to store events by content (same prompt, same text, same tool name and all arguments). The reviewer's own recount on raw rows and lines agrees event by event: 6 of 23 events with 63 statements, 7 of 24 with 64, 8 of 27 with 71. The shared store is outside the read; its tracked_file_content row states the edited file again and is not counted.

Protobuf. The vendor publishes no schema. Fields are named by number and by content. The compound shell call (inspect && baseline in one call) is scored by the compound rule: both helper output lines are in the native result, the native failure exit code 1 counts for the last segment and the unbroken && chain gives inspect 0.

Public database. The public store.db is a rebuild by stock SQLite with new content-addressed blob ids and a new page layout, at the private byte length. On a scratch copy (v2 round; the file is byte-equal in v3) integrity_check is ok, every id is the SHA-256 of its public bytes, the graph equals the private graph under the id map, no non-zero byte lies outside live structures and no private blob id survives. Every changed value is a home alias, a remapped reference, the blanked system prompt, the blanked context message (its operating-system fragment is kept), the blanked turn token (field 1.4), the zeroed blobEncryptionKey, the five blanked systemPromptFingerprint digests or the aliased plugin name. A public reader cannot verify that the private graph had the same shape.

Public safety. In 199 public files and all file names the reviewer found no home user name, home path, e-mail, account or auth id, host name, person name or token pattern (plain, case variants, UTF-16, hex, base64, URL-encoded, reversed), no phrase of the system prompt or of the injected context message (v2 round; those files are byte-equal in v3), and none of the 18 private line hashes as a token. One 7-character private hash value is by chance a substring of a SHA-256 row digest of run 3 that was already in the v1 bundle; it is not a token. check_public_packets passes with an empty allowlist; short_digest_warnings gives no finding on v3 and 18 on v2. The oracle test at depth 1 to 3 has no hit except the three public replay digests. The reviewer did not know every account id and searched the values of the two harness files and patterns.

Residual in the public extract. Two of the 18 zeroed hash values are 7 characters long, because the vendor prints no leading zero and the sanitizer keeps the byte length. This shows that the first hex digit of two private values is zero (4 bits each). If the unknown preimage covers the private path, this is a 1-in-256 check of a guess, not a confirmation. The reviewer does not hold the set for it; padding to 8 zeros at the next rebuild would remove it.

Content that stays public: session, request, message and call ids, which the vendor can map to the account; encrypted reasoning signatures; the sizes of the operator's rules, skills, MCP and subagent text (root field 5, numbers only); the time zone; the repository name and branch name; workspace file listings; times of the shared-store rows. Whether to publish these is an owner decision.

The packet manifests, replay receipts and the producer summary still say public_safe: false and independent_reproduction: false. This review is an attestation by an agent; it does not change those fields and is not an independent reproduction on a second environment. Tests that need artifact files could not run in the snapshot.
